description: Solar day, spin, year and the sentence that explains them.

expected.headline: The Sun turns once every 25.4 Earth days, but not as one piece: it is a ball of gas, so its equator laps its poles. Nothing here has a day, because there is no sunrise to count from.

A day here is longer than a year. One sunrise to the next takes 175.9 Earth days, while a full trip round the Sun takes only 88.0 Earth days, so it goes round the Sun 2.0 times between one sunrise and the next.
It spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west. A day here lasts 116.8 Earth days and a year 224.7 Earth days, which means the whole year is only 1.9 of its own days long.

A day here is 24h 00m, but one full spin takes 23h 56m. The difference is that it also moves along its orbit while it turns, so it has to turn a little further to bring the Sun back round. Those slivers add up: a year holds 365.26 days but 366.26 spins, exactly one more.

It turns in 9h 56m, faster than any rocky planet, so even though a year here lasts 11.9 Earth years it holds about 10,476 of its own days.
